metaTitle: Roofing Advertising: Google Ads, LSA and Meta Ads
metaDescription: Roofing advertising from ASP: Google Search Ads, Local Services Ads and Meta for roofers, with budgets planned around storms and tracked to booked jobs.

hero.h1: Roofing Advertising Measured by Booked Roof Jobs
hero.subhead: Reach the homeowner with a leak today and the one pricing a new roof over the next few weeks. ASP runs Google Ads, Local Services Ads and Meta for roofers.
points: Ad accounts and spend in your name
Conversion action set to real leads
Budgets that follow the storm calendar

why.heading: Ad spend that follows the roofing calendar
why.intro: Crews usually stay off roofs in bad weather, and work may be limited in northern winters, BLS notes. Budgets should rise and fall with the weeks your crews can work.

cards.title: Search Ads for leak calls
cards.body: Homeowners type the problem into Google: a leak, missing shingles, a replacement quote. One ad group per service shows whether repairs or replacements are paying.

cards.title: Meta for slow decisions
cards.body: A roof replacement is decided over weeks, which gives finished-roof photos and video time to work. A cold ad asking a stranger to book a leak repair rarely pays.

cards.title: Spend weighted to job value
cards.body: Replacements, repairs and new installs carry different values, so spend leans toward the services you most want to sell.

services.heading: Roofing ad channels we manage
services.intro: Each channel has one job, and each is judged on cost per booked job, not clicks.

cards.title: Google Search Ads
cards.body: Phrase match, presence location targeting, search partners off and branded search in its own campaign. Negatives grow weekly, including roofing job seekers and DIY searches.

cards.title: Local Services Ads
cards.body: Roofers are a Local Services Ads category in the US. You pay for leads, not clicks, and Google screens roofing businesses before their ads run.

cards.title: LSA ranking signals
cards.body: Google weighs your bid and profile quality: rating, review count, response time, photos and completed verification checks, among other factors. We manage LSA against those signals.

cards.title: Meta retargeting
cards.body: Back in front of homeowners who read your replacement page and left without calling, using before-and-after shots and finished roofs from your own jobs.

cards.title: Recruiting campaigns
cards.body: Meta reaches roofers who aren't job hunting that day. Hiring runs on its own budget, so it never muddies your lead numbers.

cards.title: Tracking to the booked job
cards.body: The conversion action stays on the lead you sell. For roofers on Housecall Pro, revenue from booked jobs can feed Google Ads bidding as an offline conversion.

stats.label: Average yearly roofer job openings projected

process.heading: From account audit to storm season

steps.title: Read the account first
steps.body: Settings, search terms, geography and what the conversion action counts. You get findings in priority order before we touch your budget.

steps.title: Fix tracking before bidding
steps.body: If the account counts page views or short calls as leads, bids chase the wrong thing. Tracking gets fixed first.

steps.title: Ready the phones
steps.body: Call coverage and message handling need to be in place before storm budgets rise, since missed calls may count against you on Local Services Ads.

steps.title: Monthly spend review
steps.body: What was spent, what it booked, what changed and why, broken out by channel.

pricing.heading: Roofing ad management packages
pricing.subhead: Paid media management is included from Growth up, covering Google Ads, Local Services Ads and Meta for your roofing company. Ad spend stays separate.

faqs.question: Are Local Services Ads worth it for roofers?
faqs.answer: For roofers who qualify, they're worth testing because you pay per lead instead of per click. Where you rank depends on reviews, response time and your bid, among other factors, so call handling is part of the job.

faqs.question: What is the Google Verified badge?
faqs.answer: It's the name Google now uses for its Local Services verification badge. Google said it would discontinue the money-back guarantee tied to the older badge, with reimbursement only for services booked before December 7, 2025, so roofing ads shouldn't promise one.

faqs.question: Do Facebook ads work for roofing?
faqs.answer: For replacements, often yes, because homeowners take weeks to decide. For emergency leaks, rarely, since those buyers search Google the moment it happens. Retargeting past site visitors is where we start.

faqs.question: How much should a roofer spend on ads?
faqs.answer: Work back from what a booked job is worth, not a flat monthly number. A replacement can carry a much higher cost per lead than a small repair and still pay. Spend goes straight to Google and Meta.

faqs.question: Which searches should roofing ads keep out?
faqs.answer: Searches such as those from people looking for roofing jobs, pricing shingles to buy or planning a do-it-yourself repair. Those go on the negative keyword list, which grows every week, so the budget stays on homeowners who want a roofer.

cta.body: Book a call and we'll go through your Google Ads and Local Services Ads with you, including where storm-season spend went and what the conversion action is counting.
